subject: physics
title: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
welcome_lead: Pull two masses together with F = G m₁ m₂ / r² and feel an inverse-square force.
meta_desc: A-Level Gravitational Fields adventure on Newton's universal law of gravitation.
final_note: From apples to planets, the same equation rules every gravitational pair.

concepts.def: F = G m₁ m₂ / r²; always attractive.
g = F / m = G M / r².
Spherical mass acts from its centre.

walkthroughs.body_html: Every pair of masses attracts. F is proportional to product of masses and inversely proportional to the square of separation r. r is measured between centres of mass.
For a planet treated as a point: g(r) = G M / r². At Earth's surface (r = 6.4 × 10⁶ m, M = 6.0 × 10²⁴ kg), g ≈ 9.8 N/kg.
If r doubles, the force becomes ¼; if r triples, force is 1/9. Plot of F against r is a 1/r² curve; against 1/r² it's a straight line through origin.

mcqs.q: Newton's law gives F proportional to:
options: 1/r²
r²
r

mcqs.q: Gravitational force between two masses is always:
options: Attractive
Repulsive
Zero
Equal to weight

mcqs.q: If the distance between two masses doubles, what happens to the gravitational force between them?
options: It quarters — gravitational force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance.
Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity does negative work.
It halves — gravitational force is inversely proportional to distance.
It doubles — more distance means more space for gravity to act through.

mcqs.q: When you push a wall, what does Newton's third law say about the wall?
options: The wall only pushes back if your force is strong enough to make it react.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
It doubles — more distance means more space for gravity to act through.
The wall exerts an equal and opposite force on you at the same instant.

mcqs.q: Why is gravitational potential energy near a planet treated as negative?
options: Because the zero is defined at infinity; objects bound to the planet have lower (negative) potential energy than at infinity.
Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity always points downwards.
Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity does negative work.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
